newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UEFA IN CHANGE OF HEART OVER 2006 WORLD CUP ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA IN CHANGE OF HEART OVER 2006 WORLD CUP ROW.

text.p: UEFA reached a truce with English soccer officials on Friday in the row over the 2006 World Cup finals.
In a meeting in London, UEFA withdrew its unequivocal support for Germany's bid and agreed to meet officials from both England and Germany in April to decide which bid to back.
While the English Football Association (F.A.) celebrated, their German counterparts welcomed the move as "fair" but said they would win anyway.
And world governing body FIFA said the decision would not make the slightest difference to the bidding process.
Friday's meeting came as a compromise after a week of mud-slinging and verbal blows.
Now UEFA will decide in December 1998 which bid to submit to FIFA, who will announce the venue in June 2000.
The latest proposal, revealed on Friday after three hours of negotiations, represents a significant change of heart on UEFA's part.
Last week they sent a fax to the F.A. saying they were openly backing Germany's bid, which has been on the table since June 1993.
The F.A. were outraged. UEFA responded by claiming their position had been clear for over two years and the F.A. knew full well of their support for Germany.
On Friday, UEFA denied they had been forced to climb down in the row, saying the situation had changed since last week and they had reviewed their position accordingly.
"Until a week ago there was only bid...UEFA had agreed to put forward one bid. Now we have two bids and we have to decide," said UEFA general secretary Gerhard Aigner.
"UEFA is doing its utmost to have a harmonious bidding process within its federation."
He said UEFA was anxious to prevent a repeat of the bitter wrangling which marred the bidding process for the 2002 World Cup, eventually awarded jointly to regional rivals South Korea and Japan.
England coach Glenn Hoddle welcomed the "excellent news"
